record.title: Guerguerat Omicron passenger restrictions with repatriation phase
record.scope: Passenger restrictions at the Western Sahara–Mauritania crossing
record.direction: Initially both directions; later a nationality- and direction-specific repatriation exception.
record.movement: Ordinary travellers, including Moroccan and other foreign passengers.
record.exceptions: Goods transport continued; from 8 December Mauritanian nationals could return to Mauritania.
record.enforcement: An on-site journalist documented the December exception; transporter interviews support the subsequent broader reopening.
record.consequences: Passenger transport remained restricted; transporters later criticised health-document costs.
record.relationship: Follows R4-AWN-003 after an intervening November opening. This record combines the December repatriation phase rather than counting it as another closure. Western Sahara’s disputed status is retained.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; not a present-day status assessment
record.official_rationale: Limit the spread of the Omicron variant.
record.context: Renewed restriction after the short November reopening. Mauritanian repatriations were allowed from 8 December; broader passenger travel resumed in April.
record.uncertainty: EFE described an intended two-week period; no automatic December expiry inferred. April reporting compresses earlier phases, which are retained separately in this record. Actual broad reopening does not mean removal of health-entry requirements.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. 30 November 2021 to 4 April 2022 spans a changing restriction regime. Partial reopening on 8 December is explicit; no single continuous all-passenger duration.
